title: Define acceptance criteria
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the solar panel cleaning track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and demonstrate define acceptance criteria

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the solar panel cleaning track. Panels are usually mounted on roofs or elevated structures and are connected to DC and AC electrical circuits. Panels can produce voltage in daylight even when the rest of the system is off. Cleaning on this track does not include electrical work, isolation of the system, opening enclosures, or cable or connector repair. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body:
Purpose and learning outcome
After this lesson, the learner can demonstrate define acceptance criteria in a routine cleaning workplace, identify limits of their authority and document the result. The following procedures are examples; always apply the approved site process and task instructions.

Detailed workplace method
Read the approved work order line by line. Separate included tasks, exclusions, client preferences, frequency and evidence obligations. Write criteria that an independent inspector can observe: for example, a specified mirror is free of visible streaks under normal room lighting, rather than “looks perfect”. Identify material limitations and pre-existing damage. Do not promise stain removal or restoration outside the agreed scope.

Safety, boundaries and escalation
Before proceeding, confirm the actual work scope, hazards, material or equipment suitability and who can authorise changes. Stop and seek direction when work is unsafe, outside training, or the requested result conflicts with a site instruction. Record facts, not assumptions.

Worked example
A property manager requests a “spotless” kitchen but the work order excludes the inside of the oven. The supervisor records oven interior as excluded, defines checks for benches, sink and appliance exteriors, and asks for written approval before any extra work.

Supervised practical
Give learners a sample scope with ten tasks, two exclusions and three ambiguous phrases. Have them create a checklist with an observable criterion and evidence type for each included task.

Assessment and corrective feedback
An assessor observes the learner and verifies: The checklist matches authorised scope, distinguishes exclusions, contains measurable observations and flags ambiguity before work begins. If any critical safety action is missed, provide coaching and require a new demonstration. Attendance alone is not proof of competence.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Read the approved work order line by line.
Separate included tasks, exclusions, client preferences, frequency and evidence obligations.
Write each criterion so that an independent inspector can observe it, and avoid vague terms such as looks perfect.
Identify material limitations and pre-existing damage before work starts.
Confirm the scope, the hazards, the suitability of materials or equipment, and who can authorise changes.
Stop and seek direction if the work is unsafe, outside your training, or conflicts with a site instruction.
Record facts rather than assumptions, and get approval from the person who can authorise any change before extra work.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: The work order is read line by line, and included tasks, exclusions and evidence obligations are separated.
Each criterion is observable and measurable, and vague terms such as looks perfect are not used.
Pre-existing damage and material limitations are identified before work starts.
Ambiguous wording is flagged, and any change is approved by the person who can authorise it.
summary: Each approved work order is read line by line, separating included tasks, exclusions, client preferences, frequency and evidence obligations.
Acceptance criteria are written so an independent inspector can observe them, such as a mirror free of visible streaks under normal lighting, rather than vague terms like looks perfect.
Material limitations and existing damage are identified, and no stain removal or restoration is promised outside the agreed scope.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which evidence or checks are essential when you define acceptance criteria?
options: An observable criterion, the written scope and exclusions, and a named person who can authorise changes
A criterion such as looks perfect, which is judged on the day by whoever is on shift
Only the client's verbal preferences, recorded on a sticky note and kept by the cleaner
A promise of stain removal or restoration beyond the agreed scope to the client on the day

knowledgeChecks.question: What should happen when the work is outside scope or cannot be completed safely?
options: Complete the extra work to keep the client happy, then record it today
Stop, do not extend the scope, and seek written direction from the authorised person
Promise the result the client asks for and report later and sort out the scope afterwards
Decide the scope yourself and tell the client afterwards and the team will follow it

knowledgeChecks.question: What kind of acceptance criterion does the lesson say to write?
options: Whatever the cleaner judges on the day
One that an independent inspector can observe, such as a mirror free of visible streaks under normal room lighting
One based on the client's mood
